title: Identifier size and timestamp field
body: uuid7_gen() shall write exactly 16 bytes whose bytes 0 to 5 hold the reserved Unix millisecond timestamp as an unsigned 48-bit big-endian integer.
rationale: RFC 9562 places unix_ts_ms first and big-endian, so byte order is time order.
criteria: With the test clock at 0x010203040506 ms the decoded bytes 0 to 5 equal 0x010203040506.

title: Version field
body: Byte 6 of every generated identifier shall carry the version 7 (0b0111) in its high nibble.
rationale: RFC 9562 version field; readers recognise the layout by it.
criteria: (byte6 & 0xF0) == 0x70 for every identifier the suites generate.

title: Variant field
body: Byte 8 of every generated identifier shall carry the variant 0b10 in its two most significant bits.
rationale: RFC 9562 variant field.
criteria: (byte8 & 0xC0) == 0x80 for every identifier the suites generate.

title: Sequence field
body: The 12-bit rand_a field (low nibble of byte 6, then byte 7) shall carry the reserved sequence value, big-endian.
rationale: RFC 9562 6.2 method 1 (fixed bit-length dedicated counter) makes identifiers of one millisecond sortable.
criteria: Identifiers generated in one millisecond decode to sequences 0, 1, 2, ... in generation order.

title: Random tail
body: The 62-bit rand_b field shall come from the 8 bytes the active RNG returns for the call: byte 8 keeps the low six bits of the first RNG byte, bytes 9 to 15 are the next seven RNG bytes unchanged.
rationale: RFC 9562 rand_b; the tail is the unguessable part of the identifier.
criteria: With a scripted RNG the scripted bytes appear in bytes 8 to 15 as specified.

title: Clock source
body: The timestamp shall be read from CLOCK_REALTIME and truncated to whole milliseconds since the Unix epoch, on each reservation attempt.
rationale: RFC 9562 unix_ts_ms is Unix time in milliseconds.
criteria: An identifier generated with the real clock decodes to a timestamp between two CLOCK_REALTIME reads taken around the call.

title: Strict monotonicity
body: Within one process, the (timestamp, sequence) pair of every successful uuid7_gen() call shall be strictly greater than the pair of every successful call that completed before it.
rationale: Time-ordered database keys must append; the platform keys LMDB records by these identifiers.
criteria: The decoded pairs strictly increase in every single-thread and per-thread sequence the suites generate, the clock stalling or going back included.

title: New millisecond
body: When the wall clock is later than the last reserved millisecond, the generator shall reserve the wall-clock millisecond with sequence 0.
rationale: RFC 9562 6.2: the counter is reset when the timestamp advances; the timestamp tracks real time.
criteria: After the test clock steps from 1000 to 1001 ms, the next identifier decodes to (1001, 0).

title: Clock stall or regression
body: When the wall clock equals or precedes the last reserved millisecond, the generator shall reserve the last reserved millisecond with the next sequence value.
rationale: RFC 9562 6.2 monotonic error checking: a clock that stalls or steps back must not reorder identifiers.
criteria: With a test clock alternating 1000 and 999 ms, 2000 identifiers decode to strictly increasing pairs.

title: Sequence exhaustion
body: When the sequence of the last reserved millisecond is 4095, the generator shall reserve the next logical millisecond with sequence 0 instead of waiting for the wall clock.
rationale: RFC 9562 6.2 counter rollover; waiting would make generation block.
criteria: With a frozen clock at 1000 ms the 4097th identifier decodes to (1001, 0) and the 8193rd to (1002, 0).

title: Ahead-of-clock bound
body: uuid7_gen() shall refuse with -3, leaving the reservation state unchanged, any reservation whose millisecond would exceed the wall clock by more than UUID7_MAX_AHEAD_MS; the bound is not applied while the clock read fails.
rationale: Borrowed milliseconds must stay bounded so a burst or an abusive caller cannot date identifiers arbitrarily far in the future.
criteria: With the state parked at now + UUID7_MAX_AHEAD_MS and sequence 4094, one more identifier is issued, then -3 twice, then success once the clock advances 1 ms.

title: Timestamp range
body: uuid7_gen() shall refuse with -3, leaving the state unchanged, any reservation whose millisecond does not fit in 48 bits.
rationale: A truncated timestamp would wrap and sort before every earlier identifier.
criteria: With the clock at 2^48 - 1 ms and the state at (2^48 - 1, 4094), one identifier is issued and the next two calls return -3.

title: Byte order is generation order
body: Two identifiers generated one after the other by one process shall compare with memcmp() in generation order.
rationale: Consumers sort and key by the raw 16 bytes (RFC 9562 6.11, 6.13).
criteria: memcmp(previous, next) < 0 for consecutive identifiers across sequence rollovers and clock steps, and in the installed-package smoke test.

title: Floor import at initialisation
body: uuid7_init() with a non-NULL previous identifier shall, after installing the RNG, raise the reservation state to at least that identifier's (timestamp, sequence) pair.
rationale: A restarted process must keep issuing identifiers after the ones it already stored, even when the wall clock is behind.
criteria: After importing (2000, 10) with the clock at 1000 ms, the next identifier decodes to (2000, 11).

title: Floor import without RNG change
body: uuid7_raise_floor() shall raise the reservation state as uuid7_init() does and shall leave the active RNG unchanged.
rationale: The newest stored key is often known only after the database opens, long after the RNG was chosen.
criteria: After importing (5000, 7) with the clock at 1000 ms, the next identifier decodes to (5000, 8) and its tail still comes from the RNG installed before.

title: Raise only
body: An imported floor older than the current reservation state shall leave the state unchanged.
rationale: No import path may rewind the generator.
criteria: Importing (2000, 10) then (1000, 50) leaves the next identifier at (2000, 11).

title: Import validation
body: An imported identifier whose version nibble is not 7 shall be refused with -2, and one whose variant bits are not 0b10 with -3, leaving the state unchanged.
rationale: Only an identifier this format produced can serve as a floor.
criteria: A version-6 import returns -2, a variant-0b01 import returns -3; the next identifier decodes to the wall clock with sequence 0.

title: Import ahead bound
body: An imported identifier dated more than UUID7_MAX_AHEAD_MS after the wall clock shall be refused with -4 by uuid7_init() and uuid7_raise_floor(), leaving the state unchanged.
rationale: A poisoned stored key or a runaway clock must be a loud error at start, never a generator dating everything in the future.
criteria: An import at now + UUID7_MAX_AHEAD_MS + 1 and one at 2^48 - 1 return -4; the next identifier decodes to (now, 0).

title: Built-in RNG source
body: The built-in RNG shall fill the request from getrandom(2) on Linux, retrying on EINTR, and shall read the remainder from /dev/urandom when getrandom(2) fails or returns no data.
rationale: RFC 9562 6.9 asks for a cryptographically secure source; the kernel CSPRNG is one.
criteria: Inspection of _default_rng() confirms the call order, the EINTR retry and the fallback.

title: RNG selection
body: uuid7_set_rng_func() and uuid7_init() shall install the given callback; NULL shall install the built-in RNG.
rationale: Callers with their own entropy source (or tests) replace the default; NULL is the way back.
criteria: A scripted callback's bytes appear in the tail after either call; after NULL the built-in RNG (forced to fail) makes uuid7_gen() return -2.

title: Use without initialisation
body: uuid7_gen() called before any RNG was installed shall install and use the built-in RNG.
rationale: Initialisation is optional; the library must work from the first call.
criteria: After a state reset, uuid7_gen() returns 0 and the identifier carries the version and variant bits.

title: Lazy installation does not overwrite
body: The lazy installation of the built-in RNG shall never replace a callback installed concurrently by uuid7_set_rng_func() or uuid7_init().
rationale: A racing first generation must not undo an explicit configuration.
criteria: Analysis of _ensure_rng_func(): the built-in RNG is stored by compare-and-swap from NULL only.

title: Entropy before reservation
body: uuid7_gen() shall obtain the random tail before it reserves a (timestamp, sequence) pair, so a failed RNG call consumes no sequence value.
rationale: A sequence value consumed by a failed call would leave a gap and waste the 4096-entry space.
criteria: After two failed calls in one millisecond, the next successful call decodes to the sequence right after the last successful one.

title: Entropy failure
body: When the active RNG returns non-zero, uuid7_gen() shall return -2 and write nothing to the output buffer.
rationale: An identifier with missing entropy must never reach the caller.
criteria: With a failing callback and with the built-in RNG forced to fail, uuid7_gen() returns -2 and the buffer keeps its previous bytes.

title: No partial entropy
body: When the built-in RNG fails, it shall zero every byte it could not fill before returning the failure.
rationale: Uninitialised or partial bytes must not look like entropy, even inside the library.
criteria: Inspection of _default_rng(): every failure return is preceded by memset() of the unfilled suffix.

title: Clock failure behaviour
body: When clock_gettime() fails, the generator shall use timestamp 0 for that attempt, keep issuing unique identifiers from the reservation state, and increment the clock-failure count.
rationale: A failed clock must not stop generation, and must not pass silently.
criteria: Inspection of _get_realtime_ms() and uuid7_gen(): the count increments, 0 is returned, the reservation continues from the state and the ahead bound is skipped.

title: Clock failure count
body: uuid7_clock_failure_count() shall return the number of clock_gettime() failures since process start, 0 on a healthy clock.
rationale: Operators alert on a non-zero value.
criteria: After a generation with the real clock the count is 0.

title: Thread safety
body: uuid7_gen() shall be callable concurrently from any number of threads; no two calls in one process shall reserve the same pair.
rationale: Server workers generate keys in parallel.
criteria: 16 threads x 100000 identifiers: every thread's sequence strictly increases and all 1.6 million identifiers are distinct.

title: Concurrent configuration
body: uuid7_set_rng_func(), uuid7_init() and uuid7_raise_floor() shall be safe to call concurrently with uuid7_gen(); each generation shall use one callback for its whole tail.
rationale: Configuration may change while workers run.
criteria: With one thread changing the RNG and re-importing a floor, 4 x 100000 identifiers are distinct and per-thread ordered; the callback pointer is loaded once per call.

title: Non-blocking generation
body: uuid7_gen() shall never block, sleep or wait for the wall clock; its only retry shall be the compare-and-swap of the reservation state.
rationale: Callers sit on request paths; a lock or a wait would couple them.
criteria: Analysis of uuid7_gen(): no lock, no sleep, no wait; the loop repeats only after a failed compare-and-swap (another thread reserved first, or the weak form failed spuriously), so some thread always progresses.

title: NULL output buffer
body: uuid7_gen(NULL) shall return -1.
rationale: A missing buffer is a caller error reported, not a crash.
criteria: uuid7_gen(NULL) returns -1.

title: NULL floor
body: uuid7_raise_floor(NULL) shall return -1.
rationale: A missing floor is a caller error reported, not a crash.
criteria: uuid7_raise_floor(NULL) returns -1.

title: Generation cost
body: On the release profile, the mean cost of one uuid7_gen() call in a single thread shall not exceed 100 ns on the reference workstation.
rationale: Key generation sits on every write path; a budget keeps it negligible.
criteria: tests/stress/stress.c, release profile, static linkage: mean cost per uuid <= 100 ns (tests/results/stress/stress_summary.tsv).

title: Burst capacity
body: The generator shall issue 4096 identifiers per logical millisecond and absorb bursts of up to 4096 x UUID7_MAX_AHEAD_MS identifiers ahead of the wall clock before refusing.
rationale: With the default bound that is 40,960,000 identifiers, far beyond any realistic burst.
criteria: Analysis of the reservation rule (UUID7-SRS-010, UUID7-SRS-011): 4096 sequence values per logical millisecond, UUID7_MAX_AHEAD_MS + 1 milliseconds before the bound.

title: Static state
body: The library's mutable state shall be static and fixed: one 64-bit reservation word, one callback pointer and one 64-bit failure counter, all atomic (24 bytes on x86-64).
rationale: A fixed footprint needs no initialisation, no teardown and no allocation.
criteria: nm on the release object lists exactly these three data objects, 8 bytes each, in .bss.

title: No dynamic allocation
body: The library shall not allocate memory: libuuid7 shall reference none of malloc, calloc, realloc, free, aligned_alloc or posix_memalign.
rationale: No hidden allocation is a platform rule; the caller owns every buffer.
criteria: nm -D --undefined-only on the release libuuid7.so lists none of them.

title: Runtime dependencies
body: The shared library shall depend on the C library only.
rationale: A foundation library (tier 1) pulls nothing else into its consumers.
criteria: readelf -d on the release libuuid7.so lists exactly one NEEDED entry, libc.so.6.

title: Language and warnings
body: The library shall be written in C11 and compile without any compiler warning under every profile of the pinned kyr-build catalog.
rationale: The catalog's warning set (release: -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wconversion ...; audit adds -fanalyzer) is the static analysis of the code.
criteria: No "warning:" line in the build logs of the six profiles (build/pipeline/build_*.log).
notes: doc=SRS; section=5.7; group=Design and implementation constraints

title: Coding standard
body: The source shall follow ecss/PAF/CODING_STANDARD.md.
rationale: One set of conventions for every repository of the platform.
criteria: The format stage passes (clang-format 18) and inspection of the naming, banner and error-handling rules finds no deviation.
notes: doc=SRS; section=5.7; group=Design and implementation constraints

title: Public surface
body: The public interface shall be the single header app/uuid7.h; every external symbol shall start with uuid7_ and every public constant with UUID7_.
rationale: One prefix per foundation library equal to its name (NAMING.md).
criteria: The abi stage passes (abi/layout.txt, KYR_ABI_*_PREFIX) and the exports are exactly the declared functions.
notes: doc=SRS; section=5.7; group=Design and implementation constraints

title: Intended reuse
body: The library shall know nothing of the platform: it shall include only C library headers and perform no I/O other than reading the entropy source.
rationale: A foundation library is reused by every tier above it.
criteria: Every #include of app/uuid7.c other than "uuid7.h" (and the test seams) names a C library or POSIX header.
notes: doc=SRS; section=5.7; group=Design and implementation constraints

title: Test seams excluded from delivery
body: The test seams of app/uuid7_test.h shall be compiled only with -DUUID7_TESTING and never into a shipped artifact.
rationale: Deterministic clocks and forced failures must not exist in production.
criteria: nm -D on the release libuuid7.so lists no uuid7_test_ symbol.
notes: doc=SRS; section=5.7; group=Design and implementation constraints

title: Entropy file handling
body: The built-in RNG shall open /dev/urandom with O_CLOEXEC and close the descriptor on every path.
rationale: A leaked descriptor would cross exec() into child processes.
criteria: Inspection of _default_rng(): open(..., O_RDONLY | O_CLOEXEC) and close() on success and on both failure paths.

title: No disclosure beyond identifiers
body: The library shall expose no state other than the identifiers it returns and the clock-failure count.
rationale: Identifiers disclose their creation time to the millisecond (RFC 9562 6.12); nothing else may leak.
criteria: Review of app/uuid7.h: no accessor of the reservation state or of the RNG.

title: Hardened artifacts
body: The release artifacts shall pass kyr-build's check_hardening.sh.
rationale: Non-executable stack, full RELRO, immediate binding, no TEXTREL, no runpath, versioned soname and an allowlisted DT_NEEDED are the platform's floor.
criteria: check_hardening.sh on build/release/libuuid7.so and libuuid7.a reports all hard checks passed.

title: Non-Linux entropy
body: Where getrandom(2) is not available (not __linux__), the built-in RNG shall read /dev/urandom only.
rationale: The library stays portable to other POSIX systems.
criteria: Inspection of the #ifdef __linux__ branches of _default_rng().

title: Platform assumptions checked at build
body: The build shall fail on a platform without 8-bit bytes or without a 64-bit uint64_t.
rationale: The layout code relies on both.
criteria: Inspection of the _Static_assert block of app/uuid7.c.

title: Code coverage
body: The integration and scenario suites shall reach at least 80% statement and 65% decision coverage of app/uuid7.c; uncovered code shall be justified by inspection.
rationale: ECSS-E-ST-40 5.8.3.5b leaves the category D figures to be agreed; these are the agreed figures (SPAP <5.5>).
criteria: tests/results/ITs/coverage/coverage-summary.json: line_percent >= 80 and branch_percent >= 65; every uncovered line is covered by an inspection record.

title: Documented interface
body: Every public symbol of app/uuid7.h shall carry a doc comment with a brief, its parameters and its return values.
rationale: The header is the user manual's reference part.
criteria: doxygen reports no warning for app/uuid7.h.

title: Error reporting
body: Every public function shall report failure through its int return value only, never through errno, abort() or a signal, and shall leave the reservation state unchanged when it fails.
rationale: Callers decide what a failure means; a library never takes the process down.
criteria: Inspection of every return path of app/uuid7.c.

title: ABI stability
body: abi/layout.txt shall describe the public ABI; a changed line shall require a new major version and a new public name a new minor version.
rationale: Consumers pin exact versions; SemVer must tell them what a bump means.
criteria: The abi and abi-exports stages of the pipeline pass.

title: Packages
body: The library shall be delivered as two Debian packages, libuuid7 (the shared object and its soname link) and libuuid7-dev (uuid7.h, libuuid7.a and the linker symlink), with SHA256SUMS and one .buildinfo per package.
rationale: The platform installs its own libraries from the debs their releases publish.
criteria: The package stage builds both debs and the package-smoke stage compiles and runs tests/package/smoke.c against them.

title: Reproducible packages
body: Building the same commit twice shall produce byte-identical packages.
rationale: A pin is a hash; the hash must be reproducible from the source.
criteria: Two consecutive utils/build_deb.sh runs write the same SHA256SUMS.

title: Build-time configuration
body: The only build-time configuration item of the delivered library shall be UUID7_MAX_AHEAD_MS (default 10000 ms).
rationale: Fewer knobs, fewer untested configurations.
criteria: Inspection of app/uuid7.h and app/uuid7.c: UUID7_MAX_AHEAD_MS is the only overridable macro that changes behaviour; UUID7_TESTING selects the test seams, __linux__ the entropy source.

title: Installation layout
body: The packages shall install include/uuid7.h, lib/libuuid7.a, lib/libuuid7.so, lib/libuuid7.so.1 and lib/libuuid7.so.<version> under /usr/local.
rationale: Consumers find the library through the default include and library paths.
criteria: The package-smoke stage extracts both debs and builds the smoke test from <prefix>/include and <prefix>/lib only.

title: UUID7_SIZE_BYTES
body: app/uuid7.h shall define UUID7_SIZE_BYTES, an unsigned integer constant equal to 16, the size of a binary identifier.
rationale: Callers size their buffers with it.
criteria: The constant equals 16 at compile time and run time.

title: UUID7_MAX_AHEAD_MS
body: app/uuid7.h shall define UUID7_MAX_AHEAD_MS, an unsigned integer constant in milliseconds, 10000 unless the build defines it.
rationale: The abuse bound is part of the contract callers reason about.
criteria: The constant equals 10000 in a default build.

title: uuid7_rng_function_t
body: uuid7_rng_function_t shall be int (*)(void* buf, size_t n): the callback fills exactly n bytes of buf and returns 0, or returns non-zero on failure; the library calls it with n = 8, possibly from several threads at once.
rationale: Callers supply their own entropy through it.
criteria: Inspection of the typedef and of the only call site, _fill_random().

title: uuid7_init
body: int uuid7_init(uuid7_rng_function_t fn, const void* last_gen_uuid7) shall install fn (NULL: the built-in RNG) and then, when last_gen_uuid7 is not NULL, import it as a floor; it shall return 0, -2 (not version 7), -3 (not variant 0b10) or -4 (beyond the ahead bound).
rationale: One start-up call configures the generator.
criteria: Each return value is produced by a test; a refused import still installs fn.

title: uuid7_raise_floor
body: int uuid7_raise_floor(const void* last_uuid7) shall import last_uuid7 as a floor without touching the RNG and return 0, -1 (NULL), -2, -3 or -4 as uuid7_init().
rationale: The floor is often known only after the database opens.
criteria: Each return value is produced by a test.

title: uuid7_clock_failure_count
body: uint64_t uuid7_clock_failure_count(void) shall return the clock-failure count, initially 0, never decreasing.
rationale: A health metric.
criteria: The count is 0 on a healthy clock.

title: uuid7_gen
body: int uuid7_gen(void* out_buf) shall write exactly UUID7_SIZE_BYTES bytes to out_buf and return 0, or write nothing and return -1 (out_buf NULL), -2 (RNG failure) or -3 (bound or range refusal).
rationale: The one generation entry point.
criteria: Each return value is produced by a test; failures leave the buffer untouched.

title: uuid7_set_rng_func
body: int uuid7_set_rng_func(uuid7_rng_function_t fn) shall install fn, or the built-in RNG when fn is NULL, and return 0.
rationale: Entropy is replaceable at any time.
criteria: A test installs a callback and NULL and observes both.

title: Library linkage
body: libuuid7.so shall carry the soname libuuid7.so.<major> and export exactly the five functions of app/uuid7.h, each as <name>@@UUID7_<major>; libuuid7.a shall provide the same functions for static linking.
rationale: Symbol versioning lets consumers detect an ABI break at load time.
criteria: The abi-exports stage passes; nm -D lists the five symbols at UUID7_1.

title: Binary-only exchange
body: The interface shall exchange identifiers only as 16-byte binary values; text formatting (the 8-4-4-4-12 hexadecimal form) and parsing belong to the caller.
rationale: Storage and transport encodings differ per consumer; a binary core keeps the library small.
criteria: Review of app/uuid7.h: no text function, no char buffer parameter.

title: Initial state
body: Before any call the reservation state shall be (0, 0), no RNG shall be installed (the built-in RNG is installed on first use) and the clock-failure count shall be 0.
rationale: Static initialisation; no constructor runs.
criteria: Inspection of the static initialisers of app/uuid7.c.
